title: Math Pathways - Supporting Student Decision-Making
before:
Considerations for Secondary Math Pathways Implementation

Math pathways work at the secondary level supports every student to learn rigorous, engaging, and relevant mathematics that will facilitate their future academic and career pursuits. To set our high school students up for success, we need to ensure they are aware of their options in mathematics and how those align with their future academic and career goals. This section includes key resources and examples for school administrative unit (SAU) leaders, school counselors, and teachers to use when planning how to ensure that students have the guidance and support they need to navigate their options.

Math Pathways Resources for Student Decision-Making

 

Student Questionnaire

This resource provides an example of how a district could gauge students’ career interests (part 1) and an example of a decision tree that a school administrative unit (SAU) could use to guide students in choosing math courses (part 2). The career alignment lists note careers supported by different math courses. Source: Ohio Department of Education.

Download the Questionnaire
Course Descriptions

This document is an example of how a school administrative unit (SAU) could describe math courses for students. Source: Ohio Department of Education.

See Example
Student Graduation Plans

This webpage provides information for school counselors and school leaders about identifying students at risk for not graduating. It includes example templates for creating graduation plans for students, which may include their pathway through mathematics courses. Source: Ohio Department of Education.

Read More

“As student's interests and aspirations evolve, we want to be sure to provide clear and easily accessible information to help them make informed decisions now.”

- Maine Math Pathways Working Group Member
Example Student Guide to Choosing Courses

This blog post has examples of processes and resources from central Texas that support students in choosing mathematics classes. It links to a central Texas student guide and to a companion guide for school counselors and educators who support students. Source: Ohio Department of Education.

Read More

District Planning Tool

School administrative unit (SAU) leaders, school counselors, and teachers can use this tool to guide discussions about supporting student decision-making about mathematics courses and pathway enrollment. Source: Ohio Department of Education.

Download the Planning Tool

notes: 2 section headers — too few for a contents list.

decisions.label: Make a bold line a real heading
decisions.why: "Considerations for Secondary Math Pathways Implementation" is a paragraph in bold type. It reads as a heading and is spaced like one, but it is not in the page's outline, a screen reader does not announce it, and the contents list cannot link to it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 1 heading is plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Give the sub-headings their rule
decisions.why: 1 sub-heading is plain bold text. The design has a treatment for them — a teal rule down the left and a line across — and it had never been used on any page, because it needs a wrapper an author would have to know about.

decisions.label: Jumbotron callouts become notes
decisions.why: 1 callout is built as a Bootstrap jumbotron, which the component list replaced with dc-note and which Bootstrap itself removed in version 5. Same content, the site's own callout.

decisions.label: Let a short row of cards reach the page edge
decisions.why: 1 row holds cards in columns that add up to less than the full twelve, so the grid stops short and the rest of the line is blank. The cards are narrower than they need to be, which makes everything inside them taller — and the page longer. Only the column widths change.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.

decisions.label: Match the heading treatments to the final levels
decisions.why: 1 heading was wearing the wrong treatment for its level — a section header round a sub-heading or the reverse — because the wrapper was chosen before the outline was finished.
